questions.question: Which regimen matches the US-labeled adult recurrent-pericarditis dosing of rilonacept?
options: 320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg every two weeks
320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg subcutaneously once weekly
160 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg once weekly
320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 80 mg once weekly
questions.explanation:
Rilonacept Loading, Maintenance and Safety

Correct answer: 320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg subcutaneously once weekly

Use the Product-Specific Schedule

**Adult rilonacept initiation is ==320 mg== once, followed one week later by ==160 mg== weekly.** Give the loading dose as two separate 160-mg subcutaneous injections on the same day.

The US indication includes recurrent pericarditis and reduction in recurrence risk in adults and children aged at least twelve years. Pediatric dosing is weight based: ==4.4 mg/kg== loading, maximum ==320 mg==, then ==2.2 mg/kg== weekly, maximum ==160 mg==.

Do not substitute anakinra daily dosing or interpret a loading-dose entry in a secondary table as an instruction to repeat it each day. The prescribing information and trial schedule resolve the administration interval.

Perform Pretreatment and Follow-Up Safety Assessment

**Do not initiate rilonacept in an active or chronic infection without appropriate assessment and management.** Evaluate TB risk, review vaccination and avoid live vaccines during treatment.

Follow infection symptoms, injection-site reactions and lipid changes. Assess cardiovascular risk and manage elevated lipids according to the appropriate lipid-treatment framework rather than assuming the inflammatory benefit removes that risk.

Avoid combining IL-1 blockers or using another potent cytokine inhibitor without an explicit expert indication and safety plan. Review pregnancy intentions, access, storage and injection technique. Symptoms improving after the loading dose do not justify doubling the interval independently or withdrawing all surveillance. Persistent pain requires reassessment of inflammation and alternatives, not automatic dose escalation. The weekly schedule is one component of a complete recurrent-disease plan that includes steroid withdrawal, objective response assessment and later discussion of treatment duration.

320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg every two weeks: This is an interval-reduction strategy rather than the standard adult initiation and maintenance regimen. Any off-label interval change needs an individualized specialist plan; the labeled schedule starts maintenance one week after loading and continues weekly.

160 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg once weekly: One hundred and sixty milligrams is the adult maintenance dose. The standard adult initiation uses a total loading dose of three hundred and twenty milligrams, rather than beginning with a single maintenance-sized injection.

320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 80 mg once weekly: A lower absolute maintenance amount can arise from weight-based pediatric calculations. The adult recurrent-pericarditis regimen uses one hundred and sixty milligrams weekly after the adult loading dose.

questions.explanationHtml:
Rilonacept Loading, Maintenance and Safety

Correct answer: B — 320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg subcutaneously once weekly

Use the Product-Specific Schedule

  • Adult rilonacept initiation is 320 mg once, followed one week later by 160 mg weekly. Give the loading dose as two separate 160-mg subcutaneous injections on the same day.
    • The US indication includes recurrent pericarditis and reduction in recurrence risk in adults and children aged at least twelve years. Pediatric dosing is weight based: 4.4 mg/kg loading, maximum 320 mg, then 2.2 mg/kg weekly, maximum 160 mg.
    • Do not substitute anakinra daily dosing or interpret a loading-dose entry in a secondary table as an instruction to repeat it each day. The prescribing information and trial schedule resolve the administration interval.

Perform Pretreatment and Follow-Up Safety Assessment

  • Do not initiate rilonacept in an active or chronic infection without appropriate assessment and management. Evaluate TB risk, review vaccination and avoid live vaccines during treatment.
    • Follow infection symptoms, injection-site reactions and lipid changes. Assess cardiovascular risk and manage elevated lipids according to the appropriate lipid-treatment framework rather than assuming the inflammatory benefit removes that risk.
    • Avoid combining IL-1 blockers or using another potent cytokine inhibitor without an explicit expert indication and safety plan. Review pregnancy intentions, access, storage and injection technique. Symptoms improving after the loading dose do not justify doubling the interval independently or withdrawing all surveillance. Persistent pain requires reassessment of inflammation and alternatives, not automatic dose escalation. The weekly schedule is one component of a complete recurrent-disease plan that includes steroid withdrawal, objective response assessment and later discussion of treatment duration.

Other Options

  • A — 320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg every two weeks: This is an interval-reduction strategy rather than the standard adult initiation and maintenance regimen. Any off-label interval change needs an individualized specialist plan; the labeled schedule starts maintenance one week after loading and continues weekly.
  • C — 160 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 160 mg once weekly: One hundred and sixty milligrams is the adult maintenance dose. The standard adult initiation uses a total loading dose of three hundred and twenty milligrams, rather than beginning with a single maintenance-sized injection.
  • D — 320 mg subcutaneously once as a loading dose, then 80 mg once weekly: A lower absolute maintenance amount can arise from weight-based pediatric calculations. The adult recurrent-pericarditis regimen uses one hundred and sixty milligrams weekly after the adult loading dose.

References

  • Rilonacept current US prescribing information, revised 2025
  • RHAPSODY randomized-withdrawal rilonacept trial, 2021

questions.question: Which interpretation of COPPS-2 is correct?
options: Colchicine reduced postoperative pericardial and pleural effusions with no additional adverse-event burden
Colchicine reduced postoperative AF but did not reduce postpericardiotomy syndrome
Perioperative colchicine reduced postpericardiotomy syndrome, with more adverse events, mainly gastrointestinal
The trial established colchicine as treatment for an already present postoperative effusion
questions.explanation:
COPPS-2: Prevention Benefit and Gastrointestinal Harm

Correct answer: Perioperative colchicine reduced postpericardiotomy syndrome, with more adverse events, mainly gastrointestinal

Identify the Timing and Endpoint

**COPPS-2 randomized patients before cardiac surgery to weight-adjusted colchicine or placebo.** Treatment began forty-eight to seventy-two hours before surgery and continued for one month afterward.

The regimen was colchicine ==0.5 mg== twice daily for patients weighing at least 70 kg and ==0.5 mg== daily for those below 70 kg. This was a trial schedule, requiring the usual clinical organ-function and interaction review.

Postpericardiotomy syndrome within three months occurred in ==19.4%== with colchicine versus ==29.4%== with placebo. The intention-to-treat secondary AF and pericardial/pleural-effusion comparisons were not statistically significant.

Compare Benefits With Tolerability and the Relevant Trial

**Adverse events occurred in ==20.0%== with colchicine versus ==11.7%== with placebo, principally from gastrointestinal intolerance.** Benefit therefore does not imply unrestricted use without patient selection.

The earlier COPPS trial started treatment on postoperative day three and reported syndrome reduction at twelve months, ==8.9%== versus ==21.1%==. Its timing and results should not be silently attributed to COPPS-2.

Discuss prophylaxis using the applicable recommendation, surgical context, renal and hepatic status, interactions and tolerance. A preventive effect on an inflammatory syndrome does not establish a drug effect on every postoperative effusion or an independent mortality benefit. Similarly, an on-treatment AF result can be informative but is vulnerable to the consequences of discontinuation and does not override the intention-to-treat comparison. Keep prevention, treatment of established inflammatory PCIS and treatment of a noninflammatory collection as separate clinical questions.

Colchicine reduced postoperative pericardial and pleural effusions with no additional adverse-event burden: COPPS-2 did not show a significant reduction in that secondary fluid outcome, and adverse events were more frequent. Its findings must not be replaced by results from a different trial or substudy.

Colchicine reduced postoperative AF but did not reduce postpericardiotomy syndrome: The primary syndrome outcome favored colchicine. The intention-to-treat AF comparison did not reach statistical significance; the on-treatment finding must not replace the randomized primary analysis.

The trial established colchicine as treatment for an already present postoperative effusion: COPPS-2 tested prevention beginning before surgery. Treatment of an established isolated postoperative collection is a distinct question with separate trial evidence.

COPPS-2 randomized perioperative colchicine prevention trial, 2014 — https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2014.11026

COPPS randomized postoperative colchicine prevention trial, 2010 — https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehq319

ESC myocarditis and pericarditis guideline, 2025 — https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehaf192
